description:
FILED s470bt (Opus, 2026-09-06) by the B6 IR conformance corpus (5 cases).
#1022 (completed) made the plain shapes work: `sub f { last }` called from a
`for` or a bare block now exits it.  Two spellings are still wrong.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL main cd34df72):

(a) the loop has a `continue` block
      sub f { next } my $n=0;
      for my $i (1..3) { $n++; f(); $n+=100 } continue { $n+=1000 }
      print "n=$n\n";
      sub g { last } my $m=0;
      { $m++; g(); $m+=100 } continue { $m+=1000 } print "m=$m\n";
    perl  n=3003 / m=1
    PCL   DIES: `Can't "next" outside a loop block` (uncaught)

(b) the string-eval spelling
      my $k=0; for my $i (1..3) { $k++; eval q{last}; $k+=100 }
      print "k=$k\n";
    perl  k=1        PCL  k=303   (the `last` is caught inside the eval and
                                   the loop runs to completion)

(c) 288-sort's matrix has one more row: a CODEREF call (`my $c = \&f;
    $c->()`) dies where perl exits the loop.

CORPUS CASES: 186-loops-exits 187-loops-exits 282-sort 288-sort
329-string-eval.

=== DONE (s473e, Opus, 2026-09-08) -- ALL THREE HALVES ===
(a) = #1161, shipped in its own commit; see that task.

(b) THE STRING EVAL -- and the finding is where the bug is NOT.  The eval
catcher was never catching the loop-control throw: it is a `handler-case` and a
`throw` is not a condition, so the throw was already passing straight through
it.  The loop simply had no frame to reach.  Verified BEFORE writing any code by
framing the same loop another way (`sub g { last }` named but not called), which
made `eval q{last}` and `eval q{next}` correct with zero runtime change.  So (b)
is one LICENCE widening: `Pl::PExpr::TokenUtils::is_string_eval_word` (an `eval`
whose next sibling is not a Block), read by BOTH `may_dyn_exit` and
`_may_dyn_exit_set`, because a sub that string-evals must frame its callers'
loops too.  `eval BLOCK` is deliberately excluded (its `last` is lexical or a
call this unit follows by name) and asserted as a negative row.

(c) THE INDIRECT CALL -- same finding again, against this task's own suspicion.
`*p-dyn-loop-frames*` is a DYNAMIC variable, so every call carries it whatever
its shape; the call path needed nothing.  `is_indirect_call_token` reads the
shape once: an `&` Cast, or a `->` whose next sibling is a Structure::List
(`$c->(â¦)`) or a Symbol (`$o->$m`).  `->[â¦]`/`->{â¦}` are subscripts, and
`->NAME` was already right by accident (the bare method name is read by the
textual name test).  SIDE EFFECT, guarded: a MODULE sub reached through a
coderef now works, because the frame is in the CALLING unit and the callee's own
unit emits the throw -- the direct named call into another unit is the only
residue left.

PRICED IN #1162's CURRENCY (the frame's `catch` costs ~4.8 MB of compile IR):
`perl-tests` goes 1 -> 167 -> 218 frames, the 94 bundled CPAN modules 0 -> 5 ->
48.  A sweep of the eight frame-heaviest files after (b) is IDENTICAL to before
(5138 passing / 170 failing) and of the eleven heaviest after (c) likewise
(5451 / 223) -- same partial-stop points, same drops.  Narrowing the
MAY-DYN-EXIT seed would have saved 6 of 166 frames and lost the
`sub f { eval q{last} }` shape (measured by removing it).

EVERY EMISSION DIFFERENCE IS THE FRAME AND NOTHING ELSE, proven rather than
asserted: with `PCL_OPT=-dyn-loop-exit` set on BOTH sides, emission-ab reads
111/111 SAME over `perl-tests` and 45/45 SAME over the differing CPAN files.

CORPUS CASES: 186-loops-exits, 187-loops-exits and 329-string-eval left
`ir-conform/known-fail.tsv`.  288-loops-exits's STDOUT now matches perl exactly
(coderef, method, sort and bare-block rows all agree); its row stays with a NEW
owner, #1247 -- the residue is the uncaught die's EXIT CODE (SBCL 1 vs perl
255), the same cause as 120-io.  282-sort was already owned by #1240.

Full sweep 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, drops 5 = census, TOTAL 18673 (+0), GATE
clean.  Companion `--jobs 1` op/loopctl.t op/eval.t op/sort.t op/sub.t: all four
read EXACTLY their blessed snapshot rows (64/3, 131/37, 183/22, 54/11), ROW DIFF
0 NEW / 0 FIXED / 0 LOST.  Guard `Pl/t/loop-exit-01.t` 27 -> 54 rows.

FILED, pre-existing and NOT fixed here: #1379 -- perl clears `$@` when an eval is
ENTERED, PCL only sets it when the eval LEAVES.
subject: SILENT WRONG / DIES (residue of #1022, found by the ir-conform corpus): loop control from a CALLED SUB dies when the loop has a `continue` block, and `eval q{last}` never reaches the loop
